analysis.title: Labor Market Watch: Oct jobs preview: No jump-scares expected
key_insights: BofA expects October nonfarm payrolls of +75k, above consensus (private: +70k), up from +29k in September.

BofA expects the unemployment rate to stay at 4.2% as the participation rate falls a tenth and household employment gains moderate after two strong months. A larger participation drop could push the rate to 4.1%.

Initial claims are exceptionally benign by historical standards and continuing claims are trending down. BofA reads this as layoffs remaining contained despite recent high-profile layoff announcements.

Strong 3Q GDP business investment should keep supporting construction and manufacturing jobs through the data-center buildout and production of AI-related equipment. BofA sees some evidence of investment strength beyond AI, and expects education and health services to keep adding jobs at a solid pace.

Downside risks to October payrolls: weekly ADP averaged about 17k in the available October prints versus about 23k in September, seasonal factors are usually unfavorable in October, and TPS visa revocations could weigh on payrolls.

BofA expects average hourly earnings to rebound to +0.3% m/m after the outsized September decline, and average weekly hours to hold at 34.4. BofA says this points to stable labor income growth that supports consumer spending but is not necessarily inflationary.
BofA's view is that the labor market slowdown is driven more by labor supply than demand.

BofA does not expect the October jobs report to move December Fed pricing much. It says markets and the Fed will stay focused on inflation, and that Chair Warsh characterizes the labor market as near full employment, emphasizing benign claims and a steady unemployment rate over weak job growth given the labor-supply shock.

tension_points.bull_case: Claims are exceptionally benign, capex strength supports construction and manufacturing jobs, and education and health services keep adding jobs. BofA forecasts +75k, above consensus.
tension_points.bear_case: Weekly ADP gains slowed to about 17k in October from about 23k in September, October seasonals are usually unfavorable, and TPS visa revocations could weigh on payrolls.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A larger drop in labor force participation would push the unemployment rate to 4.1% rather than 4.2%.
